meta.topStoryHeadline: NYC Arts Nonprofits Benefit from Mamdani's $8.4 Million in Grants
meta.topStorySummary: The city distributed more than $8.4 million across 89 organizations for project costs, marketing, space rental, and events, with Brooklyn receiving the largest share.
executiveSummary: This week’s briefing is led by money and infrastructure: New York City’s new arts grants, SVA course cuts, and ongoing federal pressure on cultural institutions.

The strongest Black-arts stories are New York-centered, including Poster House’s Black performance archive, Sanford Biggers at the Parrish, and the Peggy Cooper Cafritz collection at the Studio Museum.
On the events side, the calendar keeps the August 27–September 27 Radar while carrying forward ongoing and upcoming listings from the last update.
meta.newsDisplayModel: 1 main top story, 8 photo highlights, remaining current-week stories text-only, older stories in archive
meta.eventsCarryForwardNote: Ongoing and upcoming events from the August 19 update were retained unless superseded by the August 27 Radar; clearly expired one-time listings were removed.

events.title: New York Black and African Literature Festival
events.venue: New York Black and African Literature Festival
events.description: Three days of readings, panels, and a market bringing writers from Africa and the global Black diaspora to Harlem, free to attend. A flagship literary gathering that belongs on every member's calendar.

events.title: School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play
events.description: Jocelyn Bioh, directed by Whitney White; cast includes Patina Miller, Denée Benton, Jasmine Amy Rogers. A sharp, Tony-nominated comedy about beauty, colorism, and belonging at a Ghanaian boarding school, with a stacked Black-led cast

events.title: Aperture Loves New York (inaugural exhibition)
events.description: Group show including Dawoud Bey, Deana Lawson, Robert Frank, Diane Arbus. The influential photography institution's first exhibition in its new home features two of the most significant Black photographers working today

events.title: Dindga McCannon: Yesterday and Today
events.description: Dindga McCannon. Harlem and Bronx-raised quilt and mixed-media artist, a founding member of "Where We At" Black Women Artists and student of Jacob Lawrence, gets a rare solo show spanning five decades

events.title: In Honor of Jean-Michel Basquiat
events.description: Roger Guenveur Smith, writer, performer, and director. Acclaimed artist's meditation on Basquiat and Black genius, limited run at an independent theatre

events.title: Carib-Import #1 (Greg Tate Art Wall mural)
events.description: Francks F. Deceus. Long-running public mural on the Black immigrant experience, viewable outside museum hours

events.title: Through Motion and Repose: Expanding the Walls 2026
events.description: Studio Museum Expanding the Walls teen fellows. Culminating showcase of the Studio Museum's teen photography fellowship, a pipeline for the next generation of Black image-makers

events.title: Dreams of This Future: The Collection of Peggy Cooper Cafritz
events.description: Group exhibition, Cafritz collection. A landmark bequest from educator, patron, and civil rights activist Peggy Cooper Cafritz, anchoring the Studio Museum's first full year in its new building

events.title: Pitch Black: Haiti + Congo Revisited
events.description: Group exhibition on Haitian and Congolese diasporic art. Steady, always-worth-a-visit show at a Black-founded Brooklyn museum

events.title: Weeksville Watchnight: Spirit Sensibilities
events.description: Juju Bae and guest practitioners, short films on Africana spiritualities. A community-rooted evening at one of Brooklyn's founding Black historic sites, pairing film with spiritual practice and conversation

events.title: Common and Special Guests: To Honor the Social Justice Legacy of Harry Belafonte
events.venue: BRIC Celebrate Brooklyn! and The Action Lab, Lena Horne Bandshell
events.description: Common, 2025 Belafonte Fellow, with special guests. A free public tribute from Common, recognizing Belafonte's legacy of justice and culture, staged by a community-rooted fellowship program rather than the main festival series

events.title: Fade: Closing artist panels
events.description: Harlan Bozeman, Andina Marie Osorio, Kiah Celeste, Emmanuel Louisnord Desir, Taj Poscé, London Pierre Williams. Closing conversations with six exhibiting artists before "Fade" comes down Sept 6

events.title: Film Screening: True North: Canadian Myths and Black Power
events.description: Documentary on Montréal's Black civil rights movement. Documentary on Black diasporic history, programmed by an independent Black-focused museum

events.title: Fade
events.description: Sixth installment of the Studio Museum's "F" show series, emerging artists. Last chance to see this emerging-artist showcase before it closes

events.title: Book Launch: Reality TV for Snobs with Ali Barthwell and Josh Gondelman
events.description: Ali Barthwell, Emmy-winning writer, first Black woman to complete Second City's HouseCo program. Independent Black-owned Brooklyn bookstore hosting an Emmy-winning Black writer

events.title: Brooklyn Caribbean Literary Festival
events.venue: Multiple Brooklyn venues, in partnership with The Center for Fiction
events.description: Lorna Goodison, Esmeralda Santiago, Barbara Jenkins, and others. Five days of readings and conversation from Caribbean-born literary figures, theme "Caribbean Worlds Writing Towards the Future"

events.title: Incendiaries: The People's Flag Show 1970
events.description: Group exhibition including Faith Ringgold, alongside Jon Hendricks, Jean Toche, Yvonne Rainer, and 150+ downtown artists and activists. Revisits a landmark 1970 act of art-world protest against war, racism, and censorship, with Faith Ringgold's involvement central to the show's history

events.title: Marlon James in Conversation
events.description: Marlon James, Booker Prize-winning novelist. A rare in-person evening with one of the most significant Black novelists writing today

events.title: America, Who Hurt You?
events.venue: National Black Theatre and Theatre for a New Audience, Polonsky Shakespeare Center
events.price: Pay-what-you-can preview Sept 10; standard pricing after
events.description: Sarah Jones, directed by Eric Ting. Tony winner Sarah Jones embodies 250 years of American history in a solo show opening National Black Theatre's new season

events.title: Beyond the Stardust (world premiere)
events.description: The Illustrious Blacks with Flea Artistic Director Niegel Smith. An Afrofuturist club musical from a Lincoln Center-championed duo, blending disco, funk, and house into an immersive night of Black queer joy

events.title: Brooklyn Caribbean Literary Festival: Keynote with Sister Nancy and Tanya Batson-Savage
events.description: Sister Nancy, Tanya Batson-Savage. A dancehall legend in conversation on Caribbean sound and storytelling, part of a five-day festival centering Black and Caribbean voices

events.title: Table of Silence Project 9/11
events.description: Jacqulyn Buglisi / Buglisi Dance Theatre, 150+ dancers and musicians. 25th-anniversary public peace ritual, drawing on the legacy of San Juan Hill, the Black and Puerto Rican neighborhood displaced to build Lincoln Center

events.title: Children's Art Carnival in Harlem: The Making of Contemporary Artists
events.description: Group show honoring Harlem's Children's Art Carnival legacy. University-gallery show on a foundational Black arts-education institution, free and closing soon

events.title: That You Are Here Is No Small Thing (picture book launch)
events.venue: The Center for Fiction, with Brooklyn Caribbean Literary Festival
events.description: Traci N. Todd, illustrated by Vashti Harrison. Caldecott medalist Vashti Harrison and author Traci N. Todd trace Black American resilience through children's eyes, a strong family-facing pick

events.title: How Shakespeare Saved My Life
events.venue: Red Bull Theater at The Public Theater, Shiva Theater
events.description: Jacob Ming-Trent, writer and performer. Solo verse-and-song piece by a Black actor-playwright on Shakespeare, race, and self-reclamation

events.title: Black Lit Book Group: That's How They Get You
events.description: Damon Young, Thurber Prize-winning author, led by Greenlight bookseller Micah. Monthly series amplifying Black voices, led by an independent Brooklyn bookstore

events.title: MOTHERSHIP EIGHT Dance & Music Festival
events.venue: Richard Rodgers Amphitheater, Marcus Garvey Park
events.description: Harlem Dance Club, community performers. Free, all-ages celebration of African diasporic dance forms, from West African and stepping to swing and hip-hop, now in its eighth year

events.title: Geometries
events.description: Julie Mehretu, Alma Thomas, Jack Whitten, William T. Williams and others, curated by Thelma Golden. Thelma Golden-curated survey of geometry as visual language across major Black abstractionists

events.title: Jazz Icons: Cécile McLorin Salvant with Glenn Zaleski
events.description: Cécile McLorin Salvant, in collaboration with JAZZ HOUSE KiDS. A Grammy-winning vocalist whose work bridges jazz, blues, and baroque performs in one of downtown's most storied sacred spaces

events.title: Fall for Dance Festival — Program 1
events.description: A.I.M by Kyle Abraham, NY premiere of "In the act of undoing". Accessible $30 entry point to see a leading Black choreographer open the festival

events.title: Macbeth (season-opening new production)
events.description: Ryan Speedo Green as Banquo, Yannick Nézet-Séguin conducts. Met's season-opening production features a Grammy-winning Black bass-baritone in a major principal role

events.title: Jazzmobile Summerfest: John Coltrane Centennial Tribute
events.venue: Multiple boroughs (Grant's Tomb, Marcus Garvey Park, Bronx Music Heritage Center, and others)
events.description: Musicians TBA, part of Jazzmobile's 61st Summerfest. A citywide, free tribute marking Coltrane's centennial from the organization that has brought jazz to NYC's neighborhoods since 1964

events.title: PHILADANCO! at Fall for Dance Festival
events.description: PHILADANCO!, New York premiere of Juel D. Lane's HEIRBORNE. An homage to the Black dance pioneers who shaped American concert dance, at NYC's most accessibly priced major dance festival

events.title: Brooklyn Public Library Book Prize: Shortlist Reading & Panel
events.venue: Brooklyn Public Library, Central Library, Dweck Center
events.description: Shortlisted 2026 authors. Past winners include Blair L.M. Kelley; the shortlist reading is a low-key way to hear finalists before the festival crowds arrive

events.title: Brooklyn Book Festival
events.description: Colson Whitehead, Tracy K. Smith, Marlon James, and others. NYC's largest free literary festival, with two Pulitzer Prize-winning Black writers among this year's headliners

events.title: The Black Composer Project: From Dawn to Cosmic Night
events.description: Works by Florence Price, Margaret Bonds, H. Leslie Adams, Undine Smith Moore, Nathaniel Dett, Adolphus Hailstork, George Walker, Howard Swanson. Ultra-intimate, artist-run showcase reviving rarely performed Black classical composers

events.title: A Sustained Becoming: Studio Museum Artists in Residence 2026
events.description: Derriann Pharr, Simonette Quamina, Taylor Simmons. The first Artist-in-Residence cohort to work in the Studio Museum's new building unveils new work funded by the Glenstone Foundation

events.title: Contemporary Choreography I
events.venue: New York City Ballet, David H. Koch Theater
events.description: Kyle Abraham's "Love Letter (on shuffle)". Rare Black-choreographed work in NYCB's mainstage repertory

events.title: Revolutionary Women
events.description: Group exhibition including Black women's Revolutionary-era history. Recasts the Revolutionary era through overlooked women's lives, including materials from the New-York African Free School

events.title: Turn. Turning. TURNT.
events.description: Cynthia Oliver Company Dance Theatre. Bessie Award winner and Guggenheim Fellow's first BAM staging since 2017, on Black girlhood, the pandemic, and re-emergence

events.title: adaku, part 2
events.description: Okwui Okpokwasili and Peter Born. Continuation of a major speculative work on the transatlantic slave trade by a leading experimental artist

events.title: Ailey at New York City Center
events.description: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, world premieres by Jamar Roberts and Yue Yin. Ailey's annual holiday season anchors NYC's dance calendar; a Jamar Roberts world premiere honoring Luther Vandross is a strong member draw

events.title: HUMAN
events.description: Nehprii Amenii, music by Martha Redbone and Aaron Whitby. BAM debut for Amenii, a kaleidoscopic puppetry work on what it means to be human

events.title: Minor Music at the End of the World
events.description: Written by Saidiya Hartman, directed by Sarah Benson, featuring André Holland, Okwui Okpokwasili, film by Arthur Jafa. US premiere of a major new work from MacArthur Fellow Saidiya Hartman, likely to sell out; worth booking now

news.title: NYC Arts Nonprofits Benefit from Mamdani's $8.4 Million in Grants
news.category: Cultural policy / funding · Funding and Policy
news.summary: The city distributed more than $8.4 million across 89 organizations for project costs, marketing, space rental, and events, with Brooklyn receiving the largest share.
news.detail: A second, separate tranche of city arts money on top of the record $323.8M culture budget, aimed at smaller neighborhood organizations. Direct, local, and on-brand: the city is actively funding the small arts organizations Soirée's members run and partner with.
meta: Mayor Zohran Mamdani; NYC Department of Small Business Services; Red Hook Art Project; Fourth Arts Block; Art on the Ave

news.title: Soul satisfaction in today's Black Hamptons: Sanford Biggers's 'Drift On' at the Parrish
news.summary: Retrospective of new textile works, prints, sculpture, and site-specific installation at the Parrish Art Museum in Water Mill, through Sept 13.
news.detail: A major museum survey for one of the most significant Black contemporary artists working today, in Soirée's summer geography. Newsletter, Instagram, and member-outing material with a short runway.

news.title: From the stage to the screen, Poster House puts together a nearly lost narrative of Black performance.
news.category: Visual art / performance history · Black Artist-Focused
news.summary: "Act Black: Posters from Black American Stage and Screen" gathers 130-plus posters and pieces of ephemera from the 1870s–1970s, framing Black entertainment as labor, art, and social history; on view through Sept 6.
news.detail: Recovers a largely undocumented visual archive of Black theatrical and film history through a NYC design museum. Strong newsletter and BAC material, and a timely member outing before it closes.
meta: Poster House; associate curator Es-pranza Humphrey

news.title: School of Visual Arts Faculty "Blindsided" by Course Cuts Amid $22M Deficit
news.category: Arts education / funding · Funding and Policy
news.summary: SVA cut courses with little warning to faculty as it confronts a $22 million deficit.
news.detail: A major NYC art school under acute financial strain, with direct effects on faculty jobs and student offerings. Signals the pressure on the arts-education institutions that train Black artists in New York.

news.title: REPORTS: 'Dreamgirls' revival will not open on Broadway in Fall 2026
news.summary: The revival directed and choreographed by Camille A. Brown and produced by Jennifer Hudson has slipped from its Fall 2026 slot; producers say the project remains active and will announce a new theatre, dates, and cast.
news.detail: A high-profile Black-led Broadway musical with a first-time Black woman director-choreographer at the helm; the delay is the period's key Black theatre development. Timely, high-interest story for members; worth tracking for a future outing.

news.title: New York artist A.K. Lovelace builds future creative generations at Harlem School of the Arts
news.summary: Profile of the comic artist who has led HSA's media and design department since 2021, covering student mural, animation, and commercial-art programs and NYC partnerships.
news.detail: Portrait of a functioning Black arts-education pipeline in Harlem, not a funding crisis story. Potential partnership and programming reference point in Soirée's own backyard.
meta: A.K. Lovelace; Harlem School of the Arts

news.title: Dreams of This Future: The Collection of Peggy Cooper Cafritz
news.summary: The show drawn from Cafritz's 2018 gift of 400-plus works opened Aug 19 and runs through Feb 28, 2027; frames collecting as care and cultural stewardship.
news.detail: A flagship Black arts institution turns a landmark gift into a public argument about Black patronage. The Fall 2026 season announcement was already shared; the opening itself is new and strong for a member visit.
meta: Studio Museum in Harlem; Connie H. Choi; Kiki Teshome; Peggy Cooper Cafritz

news.summary: A possible site has emerged for the long-delayed Latino museum even as the White House presses the Smithsonian over content and funding.
news.detail: The Latino museum's fate is a bellwether for how the current administration treats identity-focused national museums, NMAAHC included. Connects directly to the Smithsonian-pressure storyline Soirée has tracked all year.

news.summary: A new residency on Ossabaw Island, historic Gullah Geechee land, will host two cohorts of six artists (fall 2026, spring 2027) with stipends and covered travel; the Suzanne Jackson Foundation funds one fellow per cohort.
news.detail: Restores an artist retreat on land central to Gullah Geechee history, with a Black artist's foundation as a named funder. Residency-model reference; Gullah Geechee cultural-land angle.

news.title: Twenty-Two Poets Laureate Awarded $1.1 Million for Community Poetry Projects
news.summary: The Academy awarded $50,000 each to 22 city, county, state, and Tribal poets laureate for local poetry projects; the adjudication panel included Cave Canem's board chair.

appointments.role: Your August 2026 Roster Roundup: Dancers and Directors on the Move
appointments.description: Monthly roundup notes Amber Harper, Andre McGregor II, and Michael Shavelle joining Dance Theatre of Harlem, plus principal and soloist promotions across ABT and international companies. Tracks new talent entering a historically Black ballet company. Fresh-talent signal at a core partner institution.

appointments.name: Academy of American Poets
appointments.role: Twenty-Two Poets Laureate Awarded $1.1 Million for Community Poetry Projects
appointments.description: The Academy awarded $50,000 each to 22 city, county, state, and Tribal poets laureate for local poetry projects; the adjudication panel included Cave Canem's board chair. Sustained private funding for civic poetry infrastructure while public arts money contracts. Funder-strategy reference; Cave Canem tie is a Black-poetry-ecosystem marker.

exhibitions.title: Aperture Loves New York (inaugural exhibition)
exhibitions.description: Group show including Dawoud Bey, Deana Lawson, Robert Frank, Diane Arbus. The influential photography institution's first exhibition in its new home features two of the most significant Black photographers working today

exhibitions.title: Dindga McCannon: Yesterday and Today
exhibitions.description: Dindga McCannon. Harlem and Bronx-raised quilt and mixed-media artist, a founding member of "Where We At" Black Women Artists and student of Jacob Lawrence, gets a rare solo show spanning five decades

exhibitions.title: Carib-Import #1 (Greg Tate Art Wall mural)
exhibitions.description: Francks F. Deceus. Long-running public mural on the Black immigrant experience, viewable outside museum hours

exhibitions.title: Through Motion and Repose: Expanding the Walls 2026
exhibitions.description: Studio Museum Expanding the Walls teen fellows. Culminating showcase of the Studio Museum's teen photography fellowship, a pipeline for the next generation of Black image-makers

exhibitions.title: Dreams of This Future: The Collection of Peggy Cooper Cafritz
exhibitions.description: Group exhibition, Cafritz collection. A landmark bequest from educator, patron, and civil rights activist Peggy Cooper Cafritz, anchoring the Studio Museum's first full year in its new building

exhibitions.title: Pitch Black: Haiti + Congo Revisited
exhibitions.description: Group exhibition on Haitian and Congolese diasporic art. Steady, always-worth-a-visit show at a Black-founded Brooklyn museum

exhibitions.title: Fade: Closing artist panels
exhibitions.description: Harlan Bozeman, Andina Marie Osorio, Kiah Celeste, Emmanuel Louisnord Desir, Taj Poscé, London Pierre Williams. Closing conversations with six exhibiting artists before "Fade" comes down Sept 6

exhibitions.title: Fade
exhibitions.description: Sixth installment of the Studio Museum's "F" show series, emerging artists. Last chance to see this emerging-artist showcase before it closes

exhibitions.title: Incendiaries: The People's Flag Show 1970
exhibitions.description: Group exhibition including Faith Ringgold, alongside Jon Hendricks, Jean Toche, Yvonne Rainer, and 150+ downtown artists and activists. Revisits a landmark 1970 act of art-world protest against war, racism, and censorship, with Faith Ringgold's involvement central to the show's history

exhibitions.title: Brooklyn Caribbean Literary Festival: Keynote with Sister Nancy and Tanya Batson-Savage
exhibitions.description: Sister Nancy, Tanya Batson-Savage. A dancehall legend in conversation on Caribbean sound and storytelling, part of a five-day festival centering Black and Caribbean voices

exhibitions.title: Children's Art Carnival in Harlem: The Making of Contemporary Artists
exhibitions.description: Group show honoring Harlem's Children's Art Carnival legacy. University-gallery show on a foundational Black arts-education institution, free and closing soon

exhibitions.title: Geometries
exhibitions.description: Julie Mehretu, Alma Thomas, Jack Whitten, William T. Williams and others, curated by Thelma Golden. Thelma Golden-curated survey of geometry as visual language across major Black abstractionists

exhibitions.title: A Sustained Becoming: Studio Museum Artists in Residence 2026
exhibitions.description: Derriann Pharr, Simonette Quamina, Taylor Simmons. The first Artist-in-Residence cohort to work in the Studio Museum's new building unveils new work funded by the Glenstone Foundation

exhibitions.title: Revolutionary Women
exhibitions.description: Group exhibition including Black women's Revolutionary-era history. Recasts the Revolutionary era through overlooked women's lives, including materials from the New-York African Free School
